blocks.text: You can onboard a single Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project for AI Security to monitor and scan the data stores to identify sensitive data, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities.
Before onboarding the GCP project, ensure you have completed the following:

blocks.item: You must have the following roles:

table: To create, modify, and delete any resource or service within the assigned scope.
To access and administer project IAM policies.
To provide AI Security access to create, update, delete, and manage custom IAM roles at the project level.
To provide permissions to create and modify Cloud Logging configurations.
To inspect service states and operations for quota and billing of a project.
Terraform state file GCP bucket project
To store the Terraform state files.
To override the service account key creation policy.
To create a custom role in the Google Admin Console to assign permissions to user, group, and domain resources. This is required for AI Security to gain read-only access to resource data.

blocks.item: Override the service account key creation policy.
See instructions.

By default, the disable service account key creation policy prevents you from creating a service account key. Override the disable service account key creation policy for the project where you want to create the service account:
Sign in to the Google Cloud Console and go to Organization policies.
Select the organization from the project picker.
See image.
Search for Disable service account key creation and click Disable service account key creation.
See image.
On the Policy for Disable service account key creation page, click MANAGE POLICY.
See image.
Under the Policy source section, select Override parent's policy.
Under the Rules section, click ADD A RULE.
See image.
In the New rule window, under the Enforcement section, select Off.
Click Done.
See image.
Click SET POLICY to apply the changes.
See image.
Ensure the status of Disable service account key creation policy is set to Not enforced.
See image.
Create a custom role in the Google Admin Console.
See instructions.
Run the following command on Google Cloud Shell or gcloud CLI:
gcloud organizations describe <ORG_ID>
Replace <ORG_ID> with your organization ID, which is required to get the directoryCustomerId.
Copy the directoryCustomerId value from the output.
See image.
Go to the Google Admin SDK Directory.
Click the API tag in the right panel and paste the copied directoryCustomerId into the customer string.
Copy the following request provided and paste it into the Request body field.

{ "roleName": "role_name", "rolePrivileges": [ { "privilegeName": "DOMAIN_MANAGEMENT", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" }, { "privilegeName": "GROUPS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" }, { "privilegeName": "USERS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00haapch16h1ysv" } ] }
Replace role_name with a desired name for the new role.
Click Execute.
You are prompted to log in again. You can see the JSON output that includes the newly created role.

{ "kind": "admin#directory#role", "etag": "\"0A0Bc2deFgHi\"", "roleId": "4123456782", "roleName": "role_name", "roleDescription": "", "rolePrivileges": [ { "privilegeName": "DOMAIN_MANAGEMENT", "serviceId": "00abcdef16g1hij" } , { "privilegeName": "GROUPS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00abcdef16g1hij" } , { "privilegeName": "USERS_RETRIEVE", "serviceId": "00abcdef16g1hij" } ], "isSystemRole": false, "isSuperAdminRole": false }
See image.
Sign in to the Google Admin Console, search for the newly created role, then click View privileges to see the assigned permissions.
See image.
The following roles are created and permissions are assigned:

table: To collect the group and member data

blocks.item: Enable the required GCP APIs in the selected GCP project.
Click to view the list of required APIs.

table: Discover Google Cloud Platform resource containers
Discover the history and inventory of Google Cloud resources
Discover cloud monitoring data and configurations
Discover governance rules on GCP resources
Manage and use API keys for Google Cloud services and APIs
Discover and classify sensitive data in BigQuery tables
Discover identity and access control for Google Cloud resources
Check connections between the virtual private cloud (VPC) network and AI Security. It is required for BYON.
Discover logs resources and perform logging operations
Discover secret manager resources and perform operations
Enable private connections between the virtual private cloud (VPC) network and AI Security
Discover Key Management Service (KMS) resources and perform KMS-related operations
Discover storage resources and read data from storage
Discover compute resources and perform compute-related operations This is required to enable notebooks.googleapis.com and compute resources on the target project.
Orchestrator, Target To enable this API, the project must be linked to billing.
Interact with Google's unified artificial intelligence and machine learning platform for AI Security to scan the AI models for vulnerabilities
Target compute.googleapis.com must be enabled on the target project to enable notebooks.googleapis.com.

blocks.item: Run the following commands in the gcloud CLI:
To set your project ID:
gcloud config set project <PROJECT_ID>
Replace <PROJECT_ID> with your project ID, which is required to authenticate your API requests and associate them with the correct project.
To enable the required API:
gcloud services enable <API_SERVICE_NAME>
Replace <API_SERVICE_NAME> with the API you want to enable.
For example, if your project ID is 812345678902, you can enable the admin.googleapis.com API by running:
gcloud config set project 812345678902
gcloud services enable admin.googleapis.com
Identify a GCP project that has the required roles and which is linked to a billing account to deploy the orchestrator template.
Install the following tools:
gcloud CLI to connect to the Google Cloud project and deploy the template using gcloud CLI. To learn more, refer to the Google Cloud documentation.
Terraform CLI v1.7.5 or later to run Terraform on a Windows system. To learn more, refer to the Microsoft documentation.
Enable debug logging (optional but recommended for troubleshooting).
See instructions.
Run the following commands to enable the debug logs:
PowerShell
$env:TF_LOG="TRACE" $env:TF_LOG_PATH="<filepath>filename.log"
Bash
export TF_LOG="TRACE" $ export TF_LOG_PATH="<filepath>filename.log"
1. Select GCP project.
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Administration > Account Onboarding.
Click Add New.
In the Start Onboarding window, select Cloud Providers.
In the Select Cloud Provider window:
For Select Cloud Type, click the GCP tile.
For Select Onboarding Type, click the Project tile.
See image.
Click Save & Next.
2. Provide GCP project details.
Provide the following details and click Save & Next.
AI Security Alias: Enter a user-friendly name for the project.
Custom Role Name Prefix: Enter a unique role name. This role name is added as a prefix to all the custom roles that are created during the onboarding process.
Service Account Prefix: Enter a unique name for the service account. This is added as a prefix to the service account created during the onboarding process.

Notification Emails (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded project. You can add up to 30 email addresses to receive notifications about the issues. You can also add email addresses after completing the onboarding process.
See image.
3. Add orchestrator details and select the network configuration.
In the Orchestrator Configuration section, provide the following GCP project details to deploy the AI Security orchestrator scanner and click Apply:
Orchestrator Project ID: Enter the project ID.
Select the Orchestrator Region: Select the region.
Orchestrator Network Configuration:

VPC Selflink: Enter the selflink of the VPC network where you want to deploy the orchestrator. The VPC selflink is the unique identifier for your VPC network in the selected region. To find the VPC and subnet selflink, run the following command on Google Cloud Shell:
gcloud compute networks describe <vpc-network-name>
See image.

Subnet Selflink: Enter the selflink of the subnet within the selected VPC where you want to deploy the orchestrator. The subnet selflink identifies the specific subnet network that is used for deployment.
See image.
4. Select services to monitor.

In the Configure Services section, select the services that AI Security must monitor and click Save & Next. AI Security permissions are restricted to monitor and scan the data only in the selected services.
See image.
5. Select regions to monitor.
In the Configure Regions section, select the regions that AI Security must monitor. AI Security creates and deploys resources required for scanning only in the selected regions.
See image.
6. Select the target projects to monitor.
In the Add Target Projects section, add the target projects that you want AI Security to monitor:
In the Add Target Projects window, enter the following information:
Project ID: Enter the project ID.
Project Name (Optional): Enter the project name.
Business Unit: Select a business unit for the project.
Click + Add Project to add more projects to monitor.
See image.
Click Save & Next.
7. Configure evidence.

AI Security discovers files and tables containing sensitive data and generates snippets of evidence data to investigate and validate the findings. You can choose an existing storage account or add a new one to store these evidence snippets. In the Evidence section, select one of the following and click Save & Next:
Custom: Enter the name of the storage account present in the orchestrator project.
Automated: AI Security creates a storage container in the orchestrator project to upload the snippet of evidence data.
See image.
8. Configure custom tags.
In the Resource Tags section, configure custom tags to identify the resources created by AI Security.
In the Resource Tags window, enter a key and value pair for the tag.
Click Add More, and enter key-value pairs to add more tags.
See image.
Click Next.
9. Deploy orchestrator.
Download and deploy the GCP onboarding template:
a. Download and modify the GCP onboarding template.
In the Deploy Orchestrator section, click GCP Onboarding to download the template as a ZIP file and extract it to a folder on your system.
Locate the backend.tf file and open it in a text editor.
Add the name of the storage bucket and a preferred prefix where you want to store the Terraform state files, then save and close the backend.tf file.
See image.
b. Deploy the GCP onboarding template.
Use any of the following methods:
Google Cloud Shell (Recommended)
Sign in to the Google Cloud Console.
On the Project Selector, select the Google Cloud project where you want to apply the Terraform configuration.
See image.
Click Activate Cloud Shell at the top.
This launches a session in the bottom pane. It can take a few seconds for the session to initialize.
See image.
From the More menu, click Upload, then select the Folder option. Click Choose Folder to select the folder containing the modified Terraform file from your system, and click the Upload button.
See image.
Run the commands to initialize the template.
gcloud CLI
Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app on your local system.
Change the current working directory to the folder containing the modified Terraform file from your system.
Run the commands to initialize the template.
c. Initialize the GCP onboarding template.
Run the following commands to initialize the template. This is required to manage your infrastructure resources.
To initialize the Terraform configuration:
terraform init
See image.
To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration:
terraform plan

When you run the terraform plan or terraform apply command, Terraform verifies that all the required APIs are enabled. If any necessary API is missing, an error message is displayed to enable it to continue. To avoid this, ensure that the required APIs are enabled in your project. To enable the necessary APIs, see Enable APIs.
For Enter a value, enter the regions where you want AI Security to monitor and scan data in the following format:
["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]
AI Security creates resources required for data scanning only in these specified regions.
See image.
To run the Terraform script and deploy resources with network analysis enabled:
terraform apply -var=‘enable_test_connectivity=true’
To deploy resources with network analysis disabled:
terraform apply -var=‘enable_test_connectivity=false’
For Enter a value, enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format:
["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]
See image.
For Do you want to perform these actions?, enter yes and then press Enter.
See image.

After the onboarding template is successfully deployed, copy the generated JSON file in the Generated JSON section and click Validate & Finish. The required resources are created in the GCP orchestrator project.
See image.
